document.title: RELECO by TURCK, Sockets — S7-M
document.revision: Undated historical catalog extract; Clearwater Tech footer; MKW mirror
document.pages: Physical PDF page 12, exact S7-M selection, wiring diagram and outline

modelingNotes: C.n denotes cable clamp and M.n denotes corresponding relay mating contact; C/M are authoring aliases. Manufacturer sequential/IEC mapping: 1=12, 2=22, 3=14, 4=24, 5=11, 6=21, 7=A1, 8=A2. IEC names describe the inserted relay's functions, not separate electrical points.

Manufacturer page 12 wiring diagram and top outline were visually inspected, including enlarged terminal legends. Outline is relay insertion/screw-access side. No geometric mapping of numbered mating apertures or underside orientation is asserted.

Represent each fixed socket conductor by an explicit project jumper C.1-M.1 through C.8-M.8. These are factory paths, not field-installed bridging. All eight paths remain mutually separate with no relay fitted. Singleton bus and connector metadata never create net continuity.

No relay coil, changeover contact, indicator, suppressor or optional bridging is included. The illustrated relay circuit only explains connection assignments. All passive socket points are application-dependent, including 7/A1 and 8/A2.

Catalog mirror specifies 10 A / 250 V, whereas historical QRC S7-M sheet https://releco.de/en/Relays-QRC/S7-M.pdf (84/0407, PDF1; text opened, diagram inaccessible) lists rated current 10 A and rated load 6 A / 250 V. Ratings conflict is unresolved; current and nominal_voltage are omitted. No AC-only assumption or installed supply is assigned.

Shared connection policy accommodates an explicit factory-path jumper plus external wiring and does not authorize arbitrary conductor stacking. No protective-earth or rail-bond connection is established by mechanical mounting. No successor or installed revision is inferred.

connectionCoverage.notes: Eight documented electrical ways, each with a screw clamp and relay mating contact, yield 16 modeled endpoints. Sequential and IEC identities are evidenced by the exact S7-M diagram and outline. No separate PE, shield, signal accessory or communications interface is documented for this bare socket. C/M distinguish sides; fixed one-to-one paths require explicit jumpers. Mating-slot coordinates are not modeled.
